articles.title: Impact Fund for Global South Creators Launches at Toronto With Focus on Distribution and Audiences (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: A new impact fund backing creators from the Global South launched at the recently concluded first edition of the Toronto Film Festival market, with a model built around getting films in front of audiences as well as getting them made.
body: “There is extraordinary work being made all over the world, and there are audiences who genuinely want to discover it,” said Archana Misra Jain, founder of The Culture Fund and CEO of Product of Culture. “But making great work is only part of the journey. So much depends on funding, distribution, strategy and people who are willing to open a door. We created The Culture Fund to bring those pieces together and to start every investment with the question most funds ask last: who is this story for, and how do we reach them?”

The launch was celebrated with a reception at TIFF Lightbox, co-hosted with the global programs arm of Women in Film, Los Angeles (WIF). Billed as WIF International + The Culture Fund Present: Celebrating Global Cinema, the event drew a mix of funders, creatives and entertainment executives, and honored Global South and diaspora filmmakers with work in this year’s Toronto Film Festival lineup.

articles.title: David Worth, Director of ‘Kickboxer’ and DP of ‘Any Which Way You Can,’ Dies at 86
articles.summary: David Worth, director of films including “Kickboxer” and DP on numerous films including Clint Eastwood’s “Any Which Way You Can,” died Sept. 4 in Sunland, Calif. He was 86.
body: Worth started out as director of photography on low-budget movies before Clint Eastwood hired him as cinematographer on “Bronco Billy” and “Any Which Way You Can,” both released in 1980.

“His work was also his joy, and his family frequently joined him on location around the world during his long career,” his daughter Christina said, “He was irreverent, funny, and in jovial spirits to the very end.”

Worth was also an author, teacher, and received his master’s degree in 2016. His books include “Milestones in Cinema: 50 Visionary Films & Filmmakers,” “Orson Welles Crash Course in Cinematography and “Zen & the Art of Independent Filmmaking (a cautionary tale).”

He is survived by his daughter, Chrystina Myers, a son, David Wertheimer, a brother and two grandsons. Van Damme remembered Worth on Instagram, writing: “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my friend David Worth. From ‘Bloodsport’ to ‘Kickboxer,’ David’s talent and vision helped create two martial arts classics that changed my life.”

articles.title: Clavicular Posts Video After Being Charged With Rape and Drugging: ‘Theres Better Ways to Make Money Then Suing Someone’
articles.summary: “Looksmaxxing” influencer Clavicular has shared his first video on social media since news circulated Monday that the online personality had been charged with rape and drugging in Massachusetts.
body: The charges against Clavicular were first filed on Sept. 8 and show that the influencer (whose real name is Braden Peters) faces one count of rape, one count of drugging someone for sexual intercourse and one count of procuring liquor for someone under 21 years of age. The alleged offenses occurred on May 23, 2025, and an arraignment is set for Oct. 14. Clavicular is not currently in custody. Clavicular’s representative, Mitchell Jackson, told NBC News that he “has not been physically served.”

While the victim was not named in accordance with Massachusetts law, reports have found that the timeline may match a civil lawsuit brought against Clavicular by 18-year-old influencer Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, who had accused him of battery, fraud and sexual misconduct in a series of events that took place in 2025. In July, Clavicular denied the allegations and filed a motion to dismiss several counts of the lawsuit.

In recent years, Clavicular has gained online attention and internet fame, notably on TikTok, thanks to provocative videos that show the 20-year-old “looksmaxxing”: injecting substances into his face, bone smashing and other practices.

articles.title: ‘The Housewife’ Review: Naomi Watts Anchors a Watchable but Underpowered True Story of Hidden Nazism in Suburban Queens
articles.summary: Long before the relevant authorities do, you’ll figure out the secret that immigrant homemaker Hermine Ryan (née Braunsteiner) holds close to her chest in “The Housewife” — a giveaway that may be the fault of some heavy-handed direction and scripting, but speaks to the detail and integrity of Naomi…
body: As an immigrant homemaker whose domestic perfectionism masks a secret, Watts' taut performance gives Ben Shirinian's debut feature tension and purpose.

“You can be anyone you want to be,” she says in praise of her new home country — our first, unsubtle clue that everything is not entirely as it appears. When New York Times reporter Joseph Lelyveld (Sheridan) turns up on her doorstep requesting to speak with her husband, she seems less surprised than you might expect: He hasn’t told her that he’s acting on a tip from famed Austrian Nazi hunter Simon Wiesenthal (an oddly sidelined figure in the film’s version of events), but perhaps she wouldn’t be entirely surprised if he did.

articles.title: Post your questions for Miranda Richardson
articles.summary: She has lit up screens large and small playing Ruth Ellis, Rita Skeeter, Barbara Castle and the hilarious Queenie in Blackadder. Alternatively, you could ask about birds of prey, orangutans or playing the cello.
body: Judging by the size of her awards cupboard, Miranda Richardson has had quite the career. She won a Bafta for the 1992 psychological drama Damage, opposite Jeremy Irons, and Golden Globes for the 1991 historical drama Enchanted April and the 1994 Nazi thriller Fatherland, and was Oscar-nominated for both Damage and the 1994 historical drama Tom & Viv. Her other notable performances include IRA member Jude in The Crying Game, Ruth Ellis in Dance With a Stranger and Lady Van Tassel in Sleepy Hollow.

She’s pretty handy at comedy, too – and probably just as familiar for playing acid-tongued Daily Prophet journalist Rita Skeeter in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, the murderous chicken-farm owner Mrs Tweedy in Chicken Run and, of course, the gloriously unhinged Queenie in Blackadder II: “I may have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but I have the heart and stomach of a concrete elephant.”

articles.title: Heart of the Beast review – Brad Pitt survivalist dogmance serves up wilderness with side of cheese
articles.summary: Pitt and loyal hound Odin get stuck in remote Alaska in this serviceable adventure with hints of Jack London and Marley & Me. One man and his dog have an amazing adventure in this survivalist drama starring Brad Pitt, from screenwriter Cameron Alexander and director David Ayer, for which the first…
body: Pitt, who last worked with Ayer on the second world war action thriller Fury, plays a US military special forces veteran called Belmont, tough, self-reliant and laconically good-humoured in the classic Pitt manner, now spending his retirement roaming the breathtaking remote landscape of Alaska in his seaplane. He is accompanied by his beloved service dog Odin, or Odey (played by four different German shepherds), who saw action with Belmont in various fuzzily imagined flashback combat sequences. Odin took retirement with Belmont and is now his best and only pal. Whether or not Belmont ever had a human partner is never revealed.

articles.title: Dolly Parton free book scheme to expand in London
articles.summary: The late singer's Imagination Library posts children a free book every month until they turn five.
body: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which posts children a free book every month until their fifth birthday, is to double the number of London boroughs it covers.
The scheme, which runs in five boroughs, will expand to 10 boroughs.
It comes a month after the country singer died at the age of 80. She set up the library in 1995 in tribute to her father, who could not read or write.
Funded by the Postcode Lottery, the expansion of the scheme will make 157,000 children eligible.

articles.title: Earl Spencer should pull Diana book from shelves, Piers Morgan says
articles.summary: Princess Diana's brother apologised to Morgan for a factual error in his memoir. Morgan said he is "pursuing legal action" against Spencer.
body: Piers Morgan has called for Earl Spencer's book about Princess Diana to be pulled from the shelves over a factual error.

Earl Spencer, Princess Diana's brother, apologised to Morgan for incorrectly describing him in the memoir as the editor of the Daily Mirror when the Mirror Group published "highly intrusive photographs of Princess Diana at the gym" in 1993.

Speaking to the BBC, Morgan said he accepted the apology but that his lawyers would be "laying out that we want the offending pages to be removed from this book. And if that means they pulp the first edition, so be it".
The BBC understands Penguin, the publishers of Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, will be amending this one point in future editions of the book.

articles.title: Mahershala Ali Agrees That Marvel’s Scrapped ‘Blade’ Reboot Is Kevin Feige’s “Biggest Failure”
articles.summary: The Marvel Studios president previously said he feels "like a gigantic loser and failure" that the project never came to fruition, and the two-time Oscar winner agrees.
body: Kevin Feige once said he feels “like a gigantic loser and failure” that Marvel ‘s planned Blade reboot never came to life with Mahershala Ali; and the two-time Oscar winner agrees.

Ali confirmed in a July interview with GQ that he would not be leading Blade, after being announced to star in the project seven years ago at Comic-Con 2019. And now, in a new profile with GQ, the actor is reiterating that he doesn’t know why the project never came to fruition.

Ali referenced comments the Marvel Studios president made during a July appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast. Feige said he was “very excited” they were able to bring in original Blade star Wesley Snipes for an appearance in 2024’s Deadpool & Wolverine, but that he felt “like a gigantic loser and failure that we didn’t get [the Blade reboot] off the ground with Mahershala.”

GQ ‘s Zach Baron read Feige’s quote back to Ali, and he said he agreed with his sentiment. “I agree with him. I agree with him one hundred percent. One hundred percent. He should feel that way. I agree,” Ali said.

articles.title: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani Slams Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: “Shameful Monument to Corruption”
articles.summary: His comments came after 12 states, including New York, and the WGA agreed to settle their antitrust lawsuits against Paramount Skydance over its bid for Warner Bros.
body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticized the Paramount -Warner Bros. Discovery merger following Monday’s settlement, calling it a “shameful monument to corruption.”
“This decision is a shameful monument to corruption and a betrayal that the American people won’t soon forget,” the mayor added.

It was revealed on Monday that 12 states, including California and New York, and the Writers Guild of America agreed to settle their antitrust lawsuits against Paramount Skydance, owned by Ellison, over its $111 billion bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, paving the way for the mega merger that will vastly reshape Hollywood.

Among the deal terms, which were announced by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led the state’s case, Paramount has committed to release a specific number of films per year, increase film production in the U.S., honor union agreements to protect workers and form a new editorial independence board “to establish guiding editorial and journalism principles” for the company’s news operations, CBS News and CNN.

articles.title: Booker Prize judges reveal shortlisted novels after selection 'tussle'
articles.summary: Past Booker winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart are among the nominees for this year's award.
body: Past Booker Prize winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart have been shortlisted for the prestigious literary award again, after a selection process that the judges described as "a tussle".
Jamaican writer James is nominated this year for his latest novel The Disappearers; while Scottish author Stuart is shortlisted for John of John.
This year's other contenders are award-winning US novelist Elizabeth Strout, and British authors M John Harrison, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry.
But seven books that appeared on the longlist in July have been jettisoned, and Dame Mary Beard, who chaired the judging panel, said agreeing on the final six "has been, to put it mildly, hard work".
